column3: The Hebrew has a singular collective man rising against us; BSB has men attacking us.
The Hebrew describes a torrent passing over our soul; BSB says the torrent overwhelmed us.
The Hebrew explicitly names our soul as the waters pass over it; BSB says they sweep us away.
The Hebrew first names our soul, has fowlers in the plural, and repeats escaped; BSB begins with we, has a singular fowler, and varies escaped with slipped away.
